title: Quantization-aware kernel routing and dequant overhead reduction
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement and validate a quantization-friendly kernel routing layer that (1) selects between INT8/FP8/mixed-precision kernels at runtime based on model and batch characteristics, (2) minimizes dequantize/requantize overhead in multi-stage attention + FFN pipelines, and (3) ties kernel selection into prefill vs decode scheduling to preserve latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel router can select an INT8 fused-attention kernel and an FP8 matmul kernel for the same model with no correctness regressions (same top-k tokens) on held-out evals
End-to-end per-token latency for decode path using quantized kernels is <= 1.15x baseline float32 for 99th percentile on target instances (A100/RTX7000-like)
Prefill throughput using INT8/FP8 mixed path shows >= 1.8x improvement in tokens/sec vs float32 baseline for common sequence lengths (32-1024)
Dequant/requant overhead reduced by 40% compared to naive pointwise dequant between attention and FFN stages
Automatic fallback to compatible kernel variant when GPU capability or model op shapes are unsupported
End-to-end integration tests + perf benchmarks added to CI, and a rollout plan in console with cost/latency flags
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
1) Add a kernel capability matrix (device compute capability, support for 8-bit fused attention, FP8 matmul kernels, supported GEMM sizes). Populate from runtime probing and feature flags.
2) Implement a lightweight routing layer that maps model op graph segments -> kernel variant (e.g., attention-fused-int8, matmul-fp8, ff-geglu-int8-mixed). Router takes runtime hints: batch_size, seq_len, is_prefill, kv_cache_hit_rate.
3) For mixed-precision paths, avoid full round-trip dequant by keeping activations in packed int8/packed fp8 buffer where possible across attention -> layernorm -> FFN boundaries. Introduce ephemeral packed buffers and fused dequantize-on-output semantics.
4) Implement a dequantization microkernel that supports bulk vectorized dequant (SIMD/CUDA warp-friendly) and supports lazy dequant when only partial outputs are used (top-k sampling).
5) Tie router to scheduler: if decode (single-step) prefers latency-optimized kernel variants; if prefill (bulk) prefers throughput-optimized variants even if they have slightly higher first-token latency.
6) Add telemetry: path chosen, dequant bytes moved, extra memcpy counts, and per-stage latencies.

Trade-offs considered:
- Maintaining packed int/float activations across stages reduces memory bandwidth but increases implementation complexity and code paths to maintain.
- FP8 kernels give better representational fidelity for some models (LLAMA-variant) but are not universally supported across GPUs; fallback layers required.
- Aggressive fusion of attention+FFN reduces kernel boundary dequantization but makes fallbacks harder and PR verification more complex.
experiments: Experiment 2026-03-04: baseline float32 attention+matmul on A100 (bs=8, seq=512): 3200 tokens/s (prefill).
Experiment 2026-03-06: int8 fused-attention + float32 matmul: 4600 tokens/s (+1.44x) but observed 18% decode P99 increase due to dequant cost at attention->FFN boundary.
Experiment 2026-03-08: int8 fused-attention + fp8 matmul with packed activation passing: 5800 tokens/s (+1.81x) and decode P99 within 1.12x baseline. Memory bandwidth utilization down ~28%.
Microbenchmark: vectorized CUDA dequant kernel reduced per-element dequant cost by 42% vs naive elementwise kernel for 32k-element tensors.
Edge-case: For small batch single-token decode on RTX-class GPUs, FP8 kernel overheads (kernel launch + conversion) dominated; we selected a different kernel variant for decode-only usage.
Quality checks: KL divergence on logit distributions between float32 and mixed INT8/FP8 path < 1e-3 across a 1k example eval set; top-1 token match rate > 99.2%
decisions: Adopt hybrid routing: prefer FP8 matmuls + INT8 fused attention in throughput-prefill mode when device supports FP8; otherwise fall back to INT8-only path.
Implement packed-activation buffers to avoid repeated dequant/requant at stage boundaries for common pipelines (attention->ln->ffn).
Do not attempt to micro-optimize for every GPU; only support optimized paths for a curated set of device families (A100, H100, RTX7000). Other GPUs will use conservative INT8 or float paths.
Expose a per-deployment feature flag to force conservative float32 fallback for critical customers until we run a canary rollout.
